messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] kinds of variables + more warnings
messages.body_plain:
The warnings aren't too hard to push through.
The big one is reassigning to a parameter because
it'll act like a local variable, not a node in the
graphical model, and I think that'll confuse people
if we don't warn them.  Naive users will also forget
to apply Jacobians when sampling a transformed
parameter.

I'm almost done with the once-per-chain derived
quantities.  We'll allow the user to specify which
parameters, transformed parameters, and derived
quantities get dumped, defaulting to just dumping
them all.

I also plan to add some variable-type abbreviations,

   boolean = int(0,1)
   categorical(K) = int(1,K)
   ordinal(K) = int(1,K)
   probability = double(0,1)
   correlation = double(-1,1)

Mainly I think they'll make the models easier to read.

I went with Gelman-and-Hill-style ordered positive
values for logit cutpoints.

   ordered(K) = vector(K) with Jacobian

JAGS uses an implicit distribution by generating K independent
values then sorting them, which is very different than what
Stan's doing -- letting each have a log differnce, starting from
zero.

- Bob

messages.subject: marginalizing out mixture responsibility
Re: [stan-dev] marginalizing out mixture responsibility
messages.body_plain:
So if we have an expression such as
foo ~ ... normal (a, b) ...
then the program knows to replace all "normal (a, b)" expressions by "N(foo|a,b)" (in bda notation).
This suggests an alternative way of writing the model, by simply having a line such as
N(foo|a,b),
which in turn clarifies the conneciton between the bugs-like model and the C++ model.
I'm not saying we need to add the normal(foo|a,b) option, I'm just working through what's happening here.  I had thought of the Bugs-like syntax as somewhat mysterious but now I'm seeing that it's just a direct recoding.
A

P.S.  I hope I used "foo" correctly above!

On Dec 27, 2011, at 5:42 PM, Bob Carpenter wrote:

> I added two mixture model examples, one for sampling
> a single value and one for estimation.
>
> They could be defined by:
>
>    z ~ bernoulli(theta); // z in { 0, 1 }
>    y ~ normal(mu[z+1],sigma[z+1]);  // index in { 1, 2 }
>
> but our discrete sampling won't be great, at least
> to start.
>
> We'll do better to just sum out z.  What we'll get is
>
>    y ~ theta * normal(mu[1],sigma[1])
>        + (1 - theta) * normal(mu[2],sigma[2])
>
> To encode this in Stan, we add the cacluated log probability
> of y to the running total.
>
> src/models/basic_distributions/normal_mixture.stan
> ---------------------------------------------------
> derived data {
>  double(0,1) theta;
>  double mu[2];
>  double(0,) sigma[2];
>
>  mu[1] <- 0.0;    sigma[1] <- 0.5;
>  mu[2] <- 4.0;    sigma[2] <- 3.0;
>  theta <- 0.25;
> }
> parameters {
>  double y;
> }
> model {
>  lp__ <- lp__
>       + log_sum_exp(log(theta) + normal_log(y,mu[1],sigma[1]),
>                     log(1.0 - theta) + normal_log(y,mu[2],sigma[2])));
> }
> ------------------------------------------------------
>
> It works pretty well (densities estimated from 1000 draws have
> roughly the right bimodal shape anyway).
>
> We use log_sum_exp(a,b) for managing overflow.  It's
> defined by
>
>  log_sum_exp(a,b) = log(exp(a) + exp(b))
>
> and the trick for managing overflow is to let m = max(a,b)
> and use
>
>  log_sum_exp(a,b) = m + log(exp(a-m) + exp(b-m))
>
> If you unwind the above example, you get the following
> term for the log probability:
>
>  log (theta * normal(y|mu[1],sigma[1])
>       + (1 - theta) * normal(y|mu[2],sigma[2]) )
>
> There's also an array version, log_sum_exp(vector<double>),
> defied by the obvious extension.
>
> I also included an estimator version with fixed variances
> for convenience:
>
>   src/models/basic_estimators/normal_mixture.stan
>
> - Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] evaluating 0 * log(0) in log probabilities
messages.body_plain:
0*log(0) comes up all the time (e.g. when assigning 0 probability to
an unobserved event), and we almost always want it to be 0, since for
most distributions we care about it makes no practical difference if
θ=0 or θ=1e-100, and the limit when approaching 0*log(0)=0.

I don't know of any (non-pathological) subtleties to do with this that
could bite us; if any exist, my opinion is that they're unlikely to
cause us more trouble than letting 0*log(0)=NaN.

Matt

messages.subject: naming variable types and mods
messages.body_plain:
I need some help finalizing naming conventions.

1.  Names of variable blocks.

Currently, we have:

   data { D }                   // per chain
   derived data { D S }         // per chain
   parameters { D }             // per leapfrog step
   derived parameters { D S }   // per leapfrog step
   model { S }                  // per leapfrog step
   generated quantities { D S } // per sample

The "S" is for where a statement goes and "D" for
where declarations go.

The "data/parameter" nomenclature is from BUGS.
Alternatives would be "known/unknown", or
"constant/variable", depending on what we want to
emphasize.

For "derived", alternatives are "transformed" or
"dependent".

An alternative to "generated quantities" would
be "cut" (from BUGS, because they are cut out of
the graphical model in the sense of not affecting
sampling), or "derived quantities" if
we go with "transformed" for the others.  I sort of
like:

   data
   transformed data
   parameters
   transformed parameters
   derived quantities

2. Variables to output

I now have output set up so that all parameters,
derived parameters, and generated quantities are output
in the order in which they were defined.

If we don't want to output all the variables (space
and time issue, mainly), then we need to somehow specify
the ones to output.

We can do that in two places: from the outside when the
model's called, or in the model itself.  The former is more
flexible and the latter faster.  I'm not sure if speed's
a big deal given that I/O is involved (it'd be something
like a std::set access).

I'm leaning toward putting it in the model rather than
in the interface to the model.  In that case, I'd
add a modifier for variable declarations that are not
to be printed, perhaps "local" (or "nuisance" for params).

- Bob

messages.subject: Stan to-do list
messages.body_plain:
We're almost there.

Here's the current to-do list, checked in as:

   STAN/doc/notes/TO-DO.txt

Everything under "TO DO" needs to be finished before
an official version 1.  Everything under "EXTENSIONS"
is slated for the future.

Some of the to-do items are easy and just here to
remind me to do them, but the commands
and R interface are still going to take a bit of work.

Let me know if there's something I missed.

I plan to knock out all the TO-DO items before
starting on the manual seriously.

- Bob

TO DO
=================================================

* check L < U in bounds

* default to random inits between -2 and 2 uniform

* make sure validation happens on inits and data

* namespace usings in StanGM
   - must be enough for all declared funs and agrads

* HMC
   - command w. specified step size, number of steps
   - include Gibbs for discrete (exact, sliced)

* command line:
   - arguments
     + help option
     + model, data, parameters
     + inits
     + num_iterations, burn_in, thin
     + refresh, progress_type
     + working_directory, clear_working_directory
     + random_seed
     X num_chains (??)
     X DIC
   - return
     + Stan object (?)

* discrete samplers:
   - Gibbs for small intervals
   - slice for others
   - what about multinomial with constraints?

* distribution engineering
   - tarball
   - basic distro site
   - check cross-platform

* include dependencies
   - top-level include headers
   - clean up dependencies

* R interface
   - simple process-level calls
     + compile model
     + dump data
     + dump inits
     + run model
     + load results
   - built-in from Rcpp
   - functions
   - attach.stan(fit)
     + traceplot(fit)
     + plot.stan(fit)
     + dump.stan(fit)
     + read.stan(file_path)

* remaining API doc

* error/exception policy throughout
   - maths
   - prob
   - matrix

* profile and optimize, at least one round

* name variable types
   - basic naming
      + data     | parameter
      + known    | unknown
      + constant | variable
   - secondary naming
      + derived, transformed, dependent
   - tertiary naming
      + generated, derived, free, cut
   - I/O modifier
      + local, nuisance
   - Andrew and Jennifer terminology
      + modeled vs. unmodeled

* disallow sampling statements in derived blocks

* remove standalone optimization algorithms

* exceptions handled by samplers
   - rejection or restart?

* merging and monitoring several threads/processes

* plug in propto calls in generator

EXTENSIONS
=================================================
* optimization
   - functor-based concept design with templates

* convergence monitoring
   - R-hat
   - n.eff (variogram, at least)
   - mean and variance of samples (per chain & across)

* forward-mode simulation
   - use when nodes can be ordered and sampled with
     all parents in graphical model defined

* benchmarks
   - agrad vs. RAD/Sacado, CppAD, ... ?
   - stan vs. MCMCpack, R, BUGS, JAGS, OpenBUGS, ...
   -

* compiler for R's linear model notation

* threading
   - rewrite memory arena as thread-local object

* interface to Python

* interface to MATLAB

* Riemannian manifold sampling
  - Girolami's method with auto-diff Hessians

* mapped distributions
   - foo(x|theta) ==> foo(xs|theta)
   - C style: x*, int size
   - iterator concept: (x.start(),x.end())
   - array concept: (x[n], x.size())

* special functions
   - inv(x) = 1/x
   - inv_square(x) = 1/(x * x)
   - dot_self(vector v);  dot_self(row_vector v);
   - log_sum_exp_ratio(vector<double> log_ratios,
                       vector<double> log_probs);
   - rank(v,s): number of components of v less than v[s]
   - ranked(v,s): s-th smallest component of v
   - interp_ln(e,v1,v2) from BUGS (whatever for?)

* random generation functions
   - rnorm(),...

* type inference & propagation
   - variable vs. constant
   - local/nuisance vs. written

* multiple imputation
   - can't do each leapfrog step
   - generated quantitities before leapfrogs

* warnings
   - a <- foo(theta) if LHS contains variable: overwrite var
   - a ~ foo(theta)  if LHS is complex expression: need Jacobian

* integer subtypes
   - integer(-inf,inf), count(1,inf), natural(0,inf)
   - boolean(0,1), categorical(1,K), ordinal(1,K),

* double subtypes
   - probability(0,1), correlation(-1,1)
   - positive(0,inf), negative(-inf,0)

* vector subtypes
   - ordered (vs. positive ordered)

* monitor/sampler interface
   - sampler, filter, aggregator, buffer
   - online means and variances
   - rHat, and split rHat
   - run in second process as we go?

* matrix slice and assign
   - index m
   - range-indexes :, a:, :b, a:b
   - e.g., matrix(M,N) m; vector(M) v;  m[,1] = v;

* conditionals
   - conditional expression
   - ternary op: cond ? x : y
   - if (cond) statement else if (cond) statement ... else statement;
   - while (cond) statement;
   - repeat statement until cond;

* multi-returns and array literals
   - (a,b,c) = foo();  // function returns array
   - (m,n,p) = (1,2,3);   // (1,2,3) is array literal

* multiple declarations
   - e.g., double a, b, c[N];

* declare and assign
   - e.g., double x = 5.0;

* extensions
   - declare file paths to #include
   - declare namespace usings
   - declare function sigs for parser

* ragged arrays
   - ready to use with vec<...<vec<x>...> pattern
   - not clear how to declare (follow C?)

* constant vari values
   - avoid placing on stack
   - how to deal with adjoints?
   - use for numeric traits
   - units 0 and 1 (scalar, vector, matrix)

* alternative distribution parameterizations
   - e.g., precision for (multi) normal
   - inverse_sqrt_gamma(...)

* subroutines
   - user-defined functions in StanGM
   - user-defined densities (how much to require?)

* compound op-assigns in StanGM
   - +=, *=, etc.

* blocking updates
   - only update subset of parameters
   - use more than one instance per sampler
   - specify blocks in program?

* complete math robustness and limits review

* restart from where command left off a la R2jags

* auto convergence monitoring -- just keep doubling (or other ratio)

* parallel random number generation necessary for MCMC?

* cut out last derivative step in leapfrog if not nec.
   - only saves if very small number of leapfrog steps

* precompiled headers to speed up model compiles

* speed measurement
   - to converge
   - time per effective sample once converged
   - time to 4 chains at 25 ESS/chain, rHat < 1.1 for all
     parameters theta[k] and theta[k]*theta[k]
   - discarding first half of samples too many if fast to converge

* automatic Jacobians
   - just specify transform
   - requires 2nd-order diff

* check each parameter shows up on LHS of ~
   - true check is run-time based on data, etc.

Stan GM MANUAL
=================================================

1.  Intro
2.  Modeling Language
     a.  basic organization
     b.  variable types
     c.  expressions: operator precedence, associativity
     d.  statements: precedence, associativity
     e.  programs
     f.  full BNF
3.  Reference
     a.  special functions
     b.  distributions
     c.  built-in variable transforms
4.  Stan Command Line
5.  Extending Stan
6.  C++ Code Generated
     a.  auto-dif
A.  Examples
     References

messages.subject: multiply_log, limiting dependencies, classes of static functions
messages.subject_clean: multiply_log, limiting dependencies, classes of static functions
messages.body_plain:
Daniel just added

   multiply_log(a,b) = a * log(b)

so that we essentially have a handle on getting
0 * log(0) right when it comes up (it also saves
space and time over the direct implementation).

I changed a couple of things in stan/agrad:

1.  I moved the multiply_log function and support
classes from agrad/agrad.hpp to agrad/special_functions.hpp
and also moved tests so the right includes happened.

I removed the #include of special_functions in agrad.

My goal is to minimize dependencies between our files
in the way of header includes.

2.  I removed some unnecessary classes.  A class that
only contains static functions can be replaced with
(inline) functions in the namespace (or an anonymous
namespace if they're only needed in the file).

Also, this lets us avoid using multiple inheritance,
which is a good thing (avoiding it, that is).

3.  I replaced the calls to calculate_log_sum_exp
in that dummy class to calls to
stan::maths::log_sum_exp(double,double).

4.  I switched the implementation from the mathematical
definition to some more efficient code and used the
more accurate log1p function:

     inline double log_sum_exp(const double& a, const double& b) {
       if (a > b)
	return a + log1p(exp(b - a));
       return b + log1p(exp(a-b));
     }

- Bob
